title: Trivial strict local inertia on generic toric characters
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-integral-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], with generic point $\eta$ and function field $K$. Let $G\to S$ be smooth, separated and of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with a commutative group law over $S$ (multiplication $G\times_SG\to G$, inverse $G\to G$ and unit $S\to G$, satisfying the group diagrams), and with semiabelian geometric fibres [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]. Let $V\hookrightarrow G_\eta$ be a closed torus subgroup over $K$ [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type] [def-weil-closed-immersion], with scalar extension as in [def-pc-base-change]. Choose a separable closure $\Omega/K$ [def-pd-separable-closure], put $\Gamma_K=\operatorname{Aut}_K(\Omega)$ with its Krull topology, and give $M=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Omega\text{-grp}}(V_\Omega,\mathbf G_{m,\Omega})$ the conjugation action [def-sfb-multiplicative-character-data]. For each $x\in S$, use the strict local field $K_x^{\mathrm{sh}}=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal O_{S,x}^{\mathrm{sh}})$ and any compatible embedding $K_x^{\mathrm{sh}}\hookrightarrow\Omega$ of [lem-dl-a1-strict-local-inertia-generic-fibres], and set $J_x=\operatorname{Aut}_{K_x^{\mathrm{sh}}}(\Omega)\subseteq\Gamma_K$. Then every $J_x$ acts trivially on $M$. This assertion concerns all points of $S$, including those of higher codimension, and any choices of the compatible embeddings.

source.place: Lan, Proposition 3.3.1.7 and §3.1.1 (character formulation of the normal-base subtorus theorem), citing Faltings–Chai I, Proposition 2.9; Lan Theorem 3.3.1.9 for the character-sheaf perspective. Local texts WANTED; online Lan thesis revised 2021, printed pp.61 and 69 read. All-point inertia formulation by the worker.

proof.text: Fix $x\in S$ and one of the specified embeddings, and put $A=\mathcal O_{S,x}$, $R=A^{\mathrm{sh}}$, $F=\operatorname{Frac}(R)\subseteq\Omega$, and $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$. Choose a Noetherian affine neighborhood of $x$. The stalk-localization statement [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] make $A$ Noetherian. It is a normal domain by the hypothesis on $S$; [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] also makes all its prime localizations normal, as required by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain]. Apply that node to the local filtered etale colimit furnished by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples]. Thus $R$ is a normal domain, is henselian, and has separably closed residue field $k$. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian] it is Noetherian. The chosen compatible embedding of its fraction field is supplied by [lem-dl-a1-strict-local-inertia-generic-fibres]. In particular, $J_x=\operatorname{Aut}_F(\Omega)$, and $\Omega$ is a separable closure of $F$.

Write $W=V_F$ and $i_F:W\hookrightarrow G_F$ for the scalar extension of $V\hookrightarrow G_\eta$, a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. After extension to an algebraic closure $\bar F$, the torus definition gives $W_{\bar F}\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$. Before applying the character theory we check that $W$ is an affine $F$-group of finite type. $G_F\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], so it is covered by finitely many affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A_j$ with $A_j$ finitely generated over $F$; by [def-weil-closed-immersion] each $i_F^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A_j)$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A_j/I_j)$, so $W$ is of finite type over $F$. The one-member family $\{\operatorname{Spec}\bar F\to\operatorname{Spec}F\}$ is an fpqc covering (a field extension is flat, and the point is the image of the affine $\operatorname{Spec}\bar F$), and the base change $W_{\bar F}\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\bar F[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$ is affine, so $W\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-affine]. Thus the torus $W$ is of multiplicative type in the sense of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], which gives a finite separable extension $E/F$ in $\Omega$ and $W_E\simeq D_E(N)$ for a finitely generated abelian group $N$. The scalar-extension character identifications in that same node and [lem-sfb-split-torus-hom-matrices], with target rank one, identify $N$ with $\mathbf Z^r$. Consequently $W_E\simeq\mathbf G_{m,E}^r$. Adjoin a finite set of field generators for $E$ and apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-set-in-finite-galois-subextension] inside $\Omega/F$ to obtain a finite Galois extension $L/F$ containing $E$. Choose a splitting $\beta:\mathbf G_{m,L}^r\xrightarrow{\sim}W_L$ and write $u_\eta=i_L\beta:\mathbf G_{m,L}^r\to G_L$, where $i_L$ is the scalar extension of $V\hookrightarrow G_\eta$.

source.place: Theorems 12.9(a), 12.18(d), Corollary 12.19, and Theorem 12.23, printed pp.233,237-240; finite normal closure: Stacks 09DT and 0EXM.

proof.text: Let $C$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite] it is finite over $R$, and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal] makes it a normal domain with fraction field $L$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian]. The finite-algebra decomposition [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product] applies to the henselian local ring $R$. Since $C$ is a nonzero domain, its only idempotents are $0,1$, so the decomposition has exactly one nonzero factor: $C$ is a henselian local ring, and its residue field $k_C$ is finite over $k$. By [lem-kun-sep-closed-finite-extension-purely-inseparable], $k_C/k$ is purely inseparable. Each $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/F)$ preserves $C$: applying $\sigma$ to a monic integral equation over $R$ gives another such equation. Its automorphism of this local ring preserves the unique maximal ideal and induces the identity on $k_C$. Indeed it fixes $k$, and in positive characteristic each $z\in k_C$ has a power $z^{p^n}\in k$, so $(\sigma z)^{p^n}=z^{p^n}$ forces $\sigma z=z$; in characteristic zero $k_C=k$.

Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $P=\mathbf G_{m,T}^r$. This split torus is separated: its diagonal is cut out by $x_i-y_i$ in $C[x_1^{\pm1},\ldots,x_r^{\pm1},y_1^{\pm1},\ldots,y_r^{\pm1}]$. It is smooth and of finite presentation, and has semiabelian geometric fibres: apply [lem-sfb-relative-torus-character-reconstruction] to the constant lattice $\underline{\mathbf Z^r}$; in each geometric fibre the abelian quotient is the trivial abelian variety. The base change $G_T$ is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change], separated and of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. It is locally of finite presentation by the tensor-algebra base-change clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition]; together with separatedness and finite type this gives finite presentation. Its commutative group diagrams and semiabelian geometric-fibre condition are preserved: the former are equalities of composites under fibre product, and every algebraically closed geometric point of $T$ composes to one of $S$ with exactly the same fibre. Both $P$ and $G_T$ therefore meet the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-normal-semiabelian-hom-extension] over the normal integral Noetherian scheme $T$. That theorem extends $u_\eta$ to a $T$-homomorphism $u:P\to G_T$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1.5, printed p.69 (PDF p.83); split torus properties: section 3.1.1; Stacks 01VB, 01KU, 01T4, 05G5.

proof.text: For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/F)$, use the $R$-automorphism of $C$ from step 3. Since both $P$ and $G_T$ are obtained by base change from $R$, pulling back $u$ along this automorphism and using their canonical identifications defines a conjugate $T$-homomorphism ${}^{\sigma}u:P\to G_T$. On the closed fibre these identifications are the identity: the induced map on $k_C$ is the identity. Hence $({}^{\sigma}u)_{k_C}=u_{k_C}$. The pointwise quotient $v=({}^{\sigma}u)u^{-1}:P\to G_T$ is a group homomorphism because $G_T$ is commutative, and its closed fibre is the identity-valued homomorphism.

source.place: Agent argument after Proposition 3.3.1.5: conjugation on a finite normalization; residue calculation of step 3.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-local-special-kernel-lifting] to the homomorphism $v$ over the nonzero Noetherian local ring $C$. It supplies a subgroup $N_0\subseteq\mathbf Z^r$ and a closed subgroup $D_C(\mathbf Z^r/N_0)\hookrightarrow P$ whose closed fibre is $\ker(v_{k_C})=P_{k_C}$ and which $v$ kills. The equality with the whole split torus forces $N_0=0$: the quotient map on closed-fibre coordinate algebras $k_C[\mathbf Z^r]\twoheadrightarrow k_C[\mathbf Z^r/N_0]$ must have zero kernel, whereas for any nonzero $n\in N_0$ it kills the nonzero element $e_n-e_0$ (the two monomials are distinct basis elements, also in characteristic two). Thus this subgroup is $P$ itself and $v$ is the identity-valued map. We have proved ${}^{\sigma}u=u$ for every $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/F)$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Corollary B.2.7, printed p.287, through the cited Noetherian local special-kernel lifting statement; the N_0=0 case is the displayed group-algebra calculation.

proof.text: Restrict the preceding equality to $L$. The subgroup inclusion $i_L:W_L\hookrightarrow G_L$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. In particular it is a monomorphism: on affine neighborhoods a map through a quotient ring is determined by its composite with the quotient map, which is surjective. It is defined over $F$, so conjugating $u_\eta=i_L\beta$ gives ${}^{\sigma}u_\eta=i_L({}^{\sigma}\beta)$. Cancelling $i_L$ yields ${}^{\sigma}\beta=\beta$. For an arbitrary $g\in J_x=\operatorname{Aut}_F(\Omega)$, normality of $L/F$ gives $g(L)=L$. After extension to $\Omega$, conjugation of the $L$-defined $\beta$ depends only on $g|_L$. Therefore ${}^{g}\beta_\Omega=\beta_\Omega$ for every $g\in J_x$.

source.place: Agent cancellation and finite Galois restriction argument; closed immersion base change: Stacks Tag 01QR (lemma-base-change-closed-immersion).

proof.text: Pullback by $\beta_\Omega$ identifies $M$ with the characters of $\mathbf G_{m,\Omega}^r$, compatibly with the $J_x$-actions, by [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality]. By [lem-sfb-split-torus-hom-matrices] these characters are precisely the Laurent monomials $t_1^{a_1}\cdots t_r^{a_r}$, $a_i\in\mathbf Z$. Every such monomial is fixed by each automorphism of $\Omega$ fixing $F$, since its coefficients are $1$ and its exponents are integers. Thus $J_x$ acts trivially on $M$. For $r=0$ this is the zero character group and the same proof applies. The chosen $x$ and compatible embedding were arbitrary, so the conclusion holds at every point, without a codimension restriction. Alternatively the conjugacy clause of [lem-dl-a1-strict-local-inertia-generic-fibres] verifies independence of the embedding directly: if $J_x$ acts trivially, then $gJ_xg^{-1}$ acts trivially, since $g h g^{-1}m=g(h(g^{-1}m))=m$.

The proof is correct. Step 1: the strict henselization R is a Noetherian, normal, henselian domain with separably closed residue field (stalk-localization, prime localizations normal, etale-colimit node, triples node, sc-strict-henselization-noetherian). Step 2: W=V_F splits over a finite Galois L/F (antiduality, hom-matrices, finite-Galois node). Step 3: C, the integral closure of R in L, is finite (032L), a normal Noetherian domain and henselian local; k_C/k is purely inseparable, so every sigma in Gal(L/F) acts as the identity on k_C, including when k is imperfect. Step 4: the hypotheses of normal-semiabelian-hom-extension hold over Spec C for P=G_m^r (relative-torus reconstruction) and for G_T (smooth, separated, finite type, finitely presented, semiabelian fibres), so u_eta extends to u. Step 5: the conjugate of u agrees with u on the closed fibre. Step 6: special-kernel-lifting gives a kernel D_C(Z^r/L) with L=0, so v is trivial. Step 7: cancelling the closed immersion i_L gives that beta is Galois-fixed. Step 8: Laurent monomials are fixed, so J_x acts trivially; the conjugacy clause covers any choice of embedding.
